question: Across Europe, about 1 in 6 Staphylococcus aureus blood infections resist methicillin. In the Netherlands, roughly what share do?
answer: About 1 in 100. Since the late 1980s Dutch hospitals have practised search and destroy: patients at risk, including anyone treated in a foreign hospital, are swabbed on arrival and isolated until cleared, and carrier staff stay off wards until treated. Parts of southern and eastern Europe run at 1 in 3 or more.
move: An average across many places says little about any one of them.
trap: Assuming a rich, crowded European country sits near the European average.
reference: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, Antimicrobial resistance in the EU/EEA (EARS-Net), Annual Epidemiological Report for 2019, 2020
